name: meta-analysis.cz data API
description: Estimate-level datasets from meta-analyses in economics and the social sciences, with the hand-coded study characteristics collected for each paper.

license.note: Cite the individual paper when you use its dataset; each entry carries its DOI.

cite_as: Havranek, T. and Z. Irsova (2026). meta-analysis.cz: data and code for meta-analyses in economics.

notes: One row per estimate, pooled across literatures.
Effects are not comparable across literatures in raw units; see effect_units. Within a literature units are consistent. Across literatures compare ratios, not levels.
Moderator columns are populated only where the source dataset recorded them; check for nulls.
source_file, effect_col and se_col identify the origin of every value, so any row can be traced to the published dataset and checked.
se_is_derived marks rows whose standard error was reconstructed rather than read directly.
Column mappings were resolved arithmetically (effect/se must reproduce the reported t-statistic) and, where that was not decisive, taken from the paper's own replication code.
Beta: the harmonisation may be revised. Pin a version, or use the DOI deposit, if you need a stable reference.

excluded.fdi: no per-estimate precision exists: the file has no standard error, t-statistic, weight or inverse-SE column, so SE-based synthesis is impossible
excluded.lags: outcome is the transmission lag (mon_bot, months to the price trough); it has no sampling standard error, so it cannot enter an effect/SE table

paper.title: Does Shareholder Activism Create Value? A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 1,973 estimates from 67 studies finds shareholder activism raises stock prices by 0% to 1.5% after correcting for publication bias.

reconciliation.note: fewer rows than the paper reports; see this dataset's note and column_mapping_verified_by for the reason (usually a missing standard error on the remainder, occasionally a published file narrower than the paper's sample)

paper.title: What Matters in Explaining the Variation in Hedge Fund Performance? A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 1,019 estimates from 74 studies identifies which factors explain the variation in hedge fund performance; net performance is near zero.
datasets.direction_note: Monthly return, not annualised.

paper.title: A Meta-Analysis of the Trade Cost Elasticity

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 3,524 estimates finds the Armington trade elasticity is 2.5-5.1 after correcting for publication bias.

paper.title: Beauty and Professional Success: A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: A meta-analysis of 1,159 estimates: the beauty premium in earnings and productivity is small once publication bias and cognitive ability are addressed.

paper.title: A Meta-Analysis of Horizontal Spillovers from FDI

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 1205 estimates finds horizontal FDI spillovers average zero, shaped by technology gap and ownership structure.
datasets.column_mapping_verified_by: determinants.do runs 'drop if aux==1' then 'drop if horiz!=1'. Applying exactly those two filters yields 1,205 usable estimates, matching the abstract exactly.

paper.title: Do Borders Really Slash Trade? A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 1,271 estimates from 61 studies finds methodological choices shrink the true border effect on trade.
datasets.direction_note: Raw coefficient on the border dummy in a log-linear gravity model; the paper's headline reduction is a transform of it, not the raw value.

paper.title: Class Size and Student Achievement: A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: A meta-analysis of 2,819 estimates from 66 studies finds little publication bias and a negligible class size effect on student achievement.

paper.title: Publication Bias in Measuring Anthropogenic Climate Change

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 48 estimates finds publication bias inflates climate sensitivity; corrected range is 1.4-2.3°C.
datasets.column_mapping_verified_by: climate.do builds prec=1/se_low and runs all FAT-PET and funnel regressions on se_low; se_up appears only in one robustness line

paper.title: Bank Competition and Financial Stability: Much Ado About Nothing?

datasets.description: A meta-analysis of 598 estimates from 31 studies finding little relationship between bank competition and financial stability.

paper.title: Individual Discount Rates: A Meta-Analysis of Experimental Evidence

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of experimental discount-rate estimates finds publication bias and a corrected mean annual rate of 0.33.

paper.title: Does Daylight Saving Save Electricity? A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: A meta-analysis of 162 estimates from 44 studies finds daylight saving time yields slight electricity savings of about 0.34%.
datasets.direction_note: Positive values denote electricity SAVINGS. The abstract writes savings as positive, the body as negative; this column follows the abstract.

reconciliation.note: fewer rows than the paper reports; see this dataset's note and column_mapping_verified_by for the reason (usually a missing standard error on the remainder, occasionally a published file narrower than the paper's sample)

paper.title: Publication Bias in Measuring the Impact of Tuition on Enrollment
paper.journal: Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 443 estimates finds the tuition-enrollment elasticity is near zero once publication bias is corrected.

paper.title: Publication Bias in Measuring Intertemporal Substitution

paper.title: Price Elasticity of Electricity Demand: A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of the price elasticity of electricity demand: no increase in price responsiveness despite ninety years of technological change.

paper.title: Do Female Directors Raise ESG Ratings? A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 533 estimates from 106 studies on whether female board directors raise corporate ESG ratings.
datasets.direction_note: Points on the Bloomberg/LSEG ESG scale per percentage point of board gender diversity, not a percent change.

paper.title: A Meta-Analysis of the Trade Effect of the Euro

datasets.description: Meta-analysis finds the euro's trade-promoting effect is insignificant once publication bias is corrected for.
datasets.direction_note: Raw gravity-model coefficient on the currency-union dummy; the headline trade effect is a transform of it.

datasets.reason: country-level crisis database, not extracted estimates

paper.title: A Meta-Analysis of the Excess Sensitivity of Consumption to Anticipated Income Changes

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 144 studies finds little excess sensitivity of consumption once micro data, publication bias, and liquidity constraints are addressed.

paper.title: Foreign Capital and Domestic Productivity in the Czech Republic: A Meta-Regression Analysis

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 332 estimates finds FDI spillovers raise Czech domestic firm productivity, larger for joint ventures.
datasets.direction_note: Winsorised FDI spillover elasticity (e_w). No standard error exists in the file, so this dataset supports model averaging over study characteristics but not SE-based synthesis.
datasets.column_mapping_verified_by: spillovers.R uses e_w (winsorized spillover elasticity) as the response in a Bayesian model averaging regression over moderators; the zip contains only that script and the data. No_of_firms is a log-scaled moderator, not a recoverable N
datasets.excluded_from_harmonised_because: no per-estimate precision exists: the file has no standard error, t-statistic, weight or inverse-SE column, so SE-based synthesis is impossible

paper.title: How Puzzling Is the Forward Premium Puzzle? A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 3,643 estimates from 91 studies finds forward rate unbiasedness holds better than commonly thought once biases are corrected.
datasets.direction_note: The null of interest is a slope of 1, not 0. Testing against zero will mislead.
datasets.column_mapping_verified_by: forward.do runs 'sum beta se' immediately after loading; T and N reproduce ln(Sample_size), so neither is a t-statistic

paper.title: Publication and Identification Biases in Measuring the Intertemporal Substitution of Labor Supply

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of over 700 estimates finds publication bias inflates the Frisch labor supply elasticity, with a corrected total hours elasticity near 0.25.

reconciliation.note: fewer rows than the paper reports; see this dataset's note and column_mapping_verified_by for the reason (usually a missing standard error on the remainder, occasionally a published file narrower than the paper's sample)

paper.title: A Meta-Analysis of the Income Elasticity of Gasoline Demand

datasets.description: Meta-regression corrects for publication bias, finding gasoline demand income elasticity of 0.1 short run and 0.23 long run.

paper.title: A Meta-Analysis of the Price Elasticity of Gasoline Demand

datasets.description: Meta-analysis shows published gasoline demand elasticities are exaggerated twofold due to publication selection bias.
datasets.direction_note: Negative by convention: demand falls as price rises.

paper.title: Habit Formation in Consumption: A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 597 estimates finds habit formation averages 0.4, with macro data yielding larger estimates than micro data.
datasets.direction_note: Unitless, normally bounded by 0 (no habit) and 1 (full persistence).

paper.title: Hedge Fund Performance: A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: Quantitative survey of 1,019 hedge fund alpha estimates from 74 studies finds little evidence of publication selection bias.
datasets.direction_note: Monthly return, not annualised.
datasets.column_mapping_verified_by: effect, se and study_id are element-wise identical across all 1,019 rows; a pairwise scan of the (effect,se) value multiset over all 41 literatures found this as the only remaining duplicate pair

paper.title: When Does Monetary Policy Sway House Prices? A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: A meta-analysis of 1,555 estimates from 37 studies across 45 countries finds publication bias exaggerates the effect of interest rates on house prices.
datasets.direction_note: Stored as a PROPORTION: house.do multiplies by 100 for the percentages the paper reports. Negative is the expected direction, higher policy rates lowering house prices. One row per impulse-response horizon, so rows within an IRF are not independent.
datasets.column_mapping_verified_by: house.do rescales est to percent and sets SE=(SE_l+SE_u)/2; seraw is populated on only 40 of 1785 rows. Restricting to inlevels==1 (the paper's own main sample) yields exactly 1,555 usable estimates, matching the abstract; the 126 growths==1 rows are a different specification.

paper.title: Financial Incentives and Performance: A Meta-Analysis of Experiments in Economics

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 2,193 estimates finds financial incentives have near-zero corrected effect on performance in most field settings.

paper.title: Optimal Inflation Rate: A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 777 estimates from 116 studies finds an optimal long-run inflation rate near 0.6% per year, below common two-percent central-bank targets.

paper.title: Transmission Lags of Monetary Policy: A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: A meta-analysis of 67 studies finds monetary policy transmission lags average 29 months, longer in developed than transition economies.
datasets.direction_note: Transmission lag: months from the monetary shock to the trough of the price response (mon_bot). A duration, not a regression coefficient, so it has no sampling standard error.
datasets.column_mapping_verified_by: lags.do keeps horizon==99 and models mon_bot directly; the se/up/low on that row belong to the price-response magnitude, not to the lag
datasets.excluded_from_harmonised_because: outcome is the transmission lag (mon_bot, months to the price trough); it has no sampling standard error, so it cannot enter an effect/SE table

paper.title: Publication Bias and P-Hacking in the Effect of COVID-19 on Learning: A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of COVID-19 learning loss: bias-corrected RoBMA and MAIVE estimates converge on about -0.12 SD, roughly 30% of a school year.
datasets.direction_note: Negative values are learning LOSS.

datasets.reason: Bartos et al. cross-field archive (external), not a Havranek literature

paper.title: Meta-Analysis Instrumental Variable Estimator
The Elasticity of Substitution between Native and Immigrant Labor: A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 1,091 estimates finds native-immigrant labor substitution elasticity rises from 13 to about 22 after bias correction.
datasets.direction_note: Stored as a negative inverse elasticity; a sign flip and inversion are needed to read it as the substitution elasticity discussed in the paper. Verify before pooling.

datasets.reason: Google Scholar search listing, not extracted estimates

paper.title: Meta-analyses of partial correlations are biased: Detection and solutions
How to Solve the Price Puzzle? A Meta-Analysis
paper.journal: Journal of Money, Credit and Banking

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 1,000 VAR estimates shows the price puzzle stems from model misspecification, not a true price effect.
datasets.effect_units: proportional change in the price level
datasets.direction_note: Stored as a PROPORTION, not a percent: multiply by 100 to read as the paper does (median |effect| 0.002 = 0.2%, consistent with its reported 0.33% trough). Positive values are the puzzling price INCREASE after a monetary contraction; theory expects negative. One row per horizon.
datasets.column_mapping_verified_by: puzzle.do computes t=res/se and prec=1/se on the long form restricted to horizon in {3,6,12,18,36}; the published file is wide, so the M{h}R / SE{h} pairs are reshaped here to reproduce it. Median |t| is 0.75-0.91 across horizons, consistent with the literature's mostly insignificant responses.
datasets.note: Same underlying data as 'lags'; excluded from the harmonised table to avoid double counting.

paper.title: Structural Reforms and Economic Growth: A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 46 studies finds structural reforms in transition countries carry short-run costs but strong long-run growth benefits.
datasets.direction_note: Computed here from the reported t-statistic and degrees of freedom, following the paper's own code.
datasets.column_mapping_verified_by: reform.do converts lib (the t-statistic on the reform coefficient, NOT a coefficient) to pcor = lib/sqrt(lib^2+df) with se_pcor = sqrt((1-pcor^2)/df); df = n - k holds exactly on all 456 rows

paper.title: Remittances and Economic Growth: A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 538 estimates finds remittances have a small positive, publication-bias-corrected effect on growth, stronger in Asia than Africa.

paper.title: Natural Resources and Economic Growth: A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 605 estimates finds weak support for the resource curse once publication bias and methods are addressed.

paper.title: Relative Risk Aversion: A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: A meta-analysis of 1,021 estimates from 92 studies finds publication-bias-corrected relative risk aversion near 1 in economics and 2-7 in finance.

paper.title: Selective Reporting and the Social Cost of Carbon

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 809 SCC estimates from 101 studies finds selective reporting creates an upward bias, especially in peer-reviewed journals.
datasets.effect_units: US dollars per tonne of carbon
datasets.column_mapping_verified_by: scc.do labels stdlow 'Standard error' and runs the funnel-asymmetry regression 'reg scc stdlow'; stdup is an alternative built from the upper CI bound for robustness

reconciliation.note: fewer rows than the paper reports; see this dataset's note and column_mapping_verified_by for the reason (usually a missing standard error on the remainder, occasionally a published file narrower than the paper's sample)

paper.title: Measuring Capital-Labor Substitution: The Importance of Method Choices and Publication Bias

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 3,186 estimates from 121 studies finds the capital-labor elasticity of substitution is 0.3, far below the literature's average of 0.9.

paper.title: A Meta-Analysis of the Relation Between Firm Size and Stock Returns

datasets.description: First meta-analysis of the size premium finds strong publication bias and a corrected effect of 1.72% in annual returns.
datasets.direction_note: Small-minus-large return spread, so positive means the premium exists; some primary studies instead report the raw size-return slope, which has the opposite sign.

paper.title: Publication and Attenuation Biases in Measuring Skill Substitution

datasets.description: Meta-analysis finds publication bias dominates in skill substitution estimates, implying a mean elasticity of 4.
datasets.direction_note: Stored as inverse elasticities; inversion is needed to read them as the skill-substitution elasticity. Dropping this step reverses the finding.

paper.title: A Meta-Analysis of Vertical Spillovers from FDI

datasets.description: A meta-analysis of 3,626 estimates finds vertical FDI spillovers to suppliers are economically significant but spillovers to buyers small.
datasets.column_mapping_verified_by: Stata_program.do runs 'drop if aux==1' and defines back = (horiz==0 & forw==0) | (horiz==0 & local==1), i.e. the non-horizontal complement

reconciliation.note: fewer rows than the paper reports; see this dataset's note and column_mapping_verified_by for the reason (usually a missing standard error on the remainder, occasionally a published file narrower than the paper's sample)

datasets.note: Same underlying data as 'bma'; excluded from the harmonised table to avoid double counting.

paper.title: Student Employment and Education: A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 861 estimates finds student employment has a negative but economically small effect on educational outcomes.

paper.title: Why Does Intertemporal Substitution Vary Across Countries? A Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 2,735 estimates across 104 countries links intertemporal substitution to income and stock market participation.
datasets.direction_note: Elasticity of intertemporal substitution. Same 2,735 estimates as the eis dataset; this file adds country-level moderators.
datasets.note: Same underlying data as 'eis'; excluded from the harmonised table to avoid double counting.

paper.title: Trust, Rule of Law, and the Size Premium: Evidence from a Meta-Analysis

datasets.description: Meta-analysis of 1,613 reported size-premium estimates from 105 studies on how generalized trust and rule of law explain the disagreement across markets.
datasets.direction_note: Raw size-return slopes: more negative means a larger conventional size premium.
datasets.column_mapping_verified_by: pairwise (effect,se) scan: 1,256 shared pairs, 276 only in size, 259 only in trust. Both papers meta-analyse reported size-premium estimates; trust is a later, extended collection (105 studies) of the same literature that size (98 studies) first assembled.

paper.title: Publication Bias in Measuring the Income Elasticity of Water Demand

datasets.description: A meta-analysis finds publication and endogeneity biases inflate reported income elasticities of water demand, with a true elasticity near 0.15.
